expectation: Membrane rings on a minority of T cells, mostly CD4 Tfh, clustered in lymphoid follicles and aggregates (germinal-centre light zones), with scattered single exhausted T cells in the stroma. Most epithelium and stroma should be negative.
observed: A: haze follows the tissue outline, with bright edges, a stripe artefact and speckle off the tissue. B: diffuse haze plus a few blobs. C: glow along the gland lumen edge and debris. D: one out-of-focus blob. E: PD1 is a reticular texture lying between the CD4 cells, not on them.
why: The signal follows tissue texture, edges and debris rather than a cell population, and in row E it does not sit on CD4 cells.
notes: The PD1 channel shows haze tied to the tissue, edge glow and bright debris, with no membrane-ringed cells. Next to clearly stained CD4 cells, PD1 lights the network between them rather than a subset of those cells.
